title: Justice and Judgment
notes: This chunk strongly assembles justice and judgment as the same Hebrew pair (tsedaqah/mishpat) rendered as commandments done, especially the due of the widow, fatherless, stranger, and poor. The recovery of “judge” as rule, deliver, and covenant-kingship is dense and law-positive, with clean use of Job, Ezekiel, Isaiah, and the Day as application of Sinai rather than alien terror. Residual house-style defects are limited to sentence-open And/That, two light presenter cues (“watch,” “Read with”), and one count written in words. No doctrine, quote, or symbol problems appear; the voice stays assertive and the evidence-to-claim seams are mostly tight.

This chunk delivers a dense, law-positive definition of justice and judgment drawn straight from the first uses and God’s own first-person statements, with clean symbolic linkage to way, truth, and peace. The closing definitions and transition to the perfect law of liberty keep the author’s assertive voice and density. One hard house-style violation appears: an author-prose sentence opens with And. No grammar errors, AI staging, stock vocabulary, or factual mismatches are present; the rest of the prose is already tight.

proposals.old: And Isaiah puts both renderings in a single verse: __“Keep ye judgment, and do *justice*: for my salvation is near to come, and my sym:sym-righteousness[righteousness] to be revealed”__ (Isaiah 56:1).
proposals.new: Isaiah puts both renderings in a single verse: __“Keep ye judgment, and do *justice*: for my salvation is near to come, and my sym:sym-righteousness[righteousness] to be revealed”__ (Isaiah 56:1).
proposals.summary: Remove prohibited And-start in author prose.
proposals.rationale: House style forbids author sentences beginning with And. Dropping the conjunction keeps the claim and the following quote intact.

proposals.old: That is why justice can be commanded, learned, and performed.
proposals.new: Justice can therefore be commanded, learned, and performed.
proposals.rationale: Author prose may not open with That. The replacement preserves the causal force without hedging or lengthening.

proposals.old: Now __“judgment”__ — Hebrew _mishpat_ — and watch what company it keeps.
proposals.new: Now __“judgment”__ — Hebrew _mishpat_ — and the company it keeps.
proposals.rationale: “Watch what company it keeps” is presenter staging. The revised line stays in the author’s voice and leads cleanly into Moses’ usage.

proposals.old: That is why judgment can be __“kept”__: to keep judgment is to render what God’s rulings say is owed.
proposals.new: Judgment can therefore be __“kept”__: to keep judgment is to render what God’s rulings say is owed.
proposals.rationale: House style bars That at the head of author sentences. “Therefore” keeps the logical link without meta-talk.

proposals.old: And God sets the crown on this meaning with a definition this book could not improve upon:
proposals.new: God sets the crown on this meaning with a definition this book could not improve upon:
proposals.rationale: Author prose cannot open with And. The rest of the sentence and the following Jeremiah definition remain unchanged.

proposals.old: Read with that office in view, Scripture does with this word what our English no longer permits.
proposals.new: With that office in view, Scripture does with this word what our English no longer permits.
proposals.rationale: “Read with…” is a presenter cue. Opening on the prepositional phrase keeps the claim and density.

proposals.old: And judgment is a thing _given to_ the saints as an inheritance: __“*judgment was given* to the saints of the most High; and the time came that the saints *possessed the kingdom*”__ (Daniel 7:22) — thrones, in Revelation’s replay of that scene: __“I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and *judgment was given* unto them… and they lived and *reigned* with Christ”__ (Revelation 20:4); __“ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, *judging* the twelve tribes of Israel”__ (Matthew 19:28).
proposals.new: Judgment is a thing _given to_ the saints as an inheritance: __“*judgment was given* to the saints of the most High; and the time came that the saints *possessed the kingdom*”__ (Daniel 7:22) — thrones, in Revelation’s replay of that scene: __“I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and *judgment was given* unto them… and they lived and *reigned* with Christ”__ (Revelation 20:4); __“ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, *judging* the twelve tribes of Israel”__ (Matthew 19:28).
proposals.summary: Remove prohibited And-start on the inheritance claim.
proposals.rationale: House style forbids And at the start of author prose. The long evidence chain after the colon is left untouched.

proposals.old: The word __“judgment”__ falls in over four hundred verses; gather them, and both words come back from Scripture defined — and joined.
proposals.new: The word __“judgment”__ falls in over 400 verses; gather them, and both words come back from Scripture defined — and joined.
proposals.summary: Render the count as digits per house style.
proposals.rationale: House style requires digits for counts. “400” matches the pattern used for other tallies without altering meaning.

proposals.new: When God names His own works, this is it:

proposals.rationale: House style forbids author sentences that begin with And. Removing it leaves a clean, assertive opening that matches the surrounding register.
